key_insight: The paper shows that RGB-D segmentation models can be made far more reliable under real-world sensor failures by training them to handle missing modalities during continued training. A simple condition dropout strategy helps the model learn to use whichever input remains available.
problem_solved: It addresses the common deployment problem where one modality (RGB or depth) is missing due to sensor failure, occlusion, or corruption. Standard RGB-D models trained only on full inputs often collapse in these partial-modality cases.
method: Introduces Condition Dropout (ConD), a continued-training paradigm that randomly removes one modality during training.
Forces the model to learn robust representations from RGB-only, depth-only, and full-modality inputs.
Improves resilience at inference time when one sensor is unavailable, without changing the core RGB-D segmentation architecture.
impact: This makes RGB-D segmentation more practical for robotics, surveillance, and autonomous systems where sensors are not always reliable. Practitioners gain a simple training add-on that can reduce performance drops under missing-input conditions.
visual_elements: A before/after pipeline showing full-modality training versus condition dropout training

paper_title: Toward Reliable RGB-D Semantic Segmentation: Handling Missing Modalities via Condition Dropout
paper_authors: Xuchen Zhu, Yajuan Wei, Shuang Hao, Jiwei Jiang, Guanxiang Mao
